metric.definition: Order-to-delivery time for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators.

reading.body:
Critical equipment lead times now gate data center construction schedules as hard as permits do.

The equipment in question is transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators. Order-to-delivery times for these items stretched from months to years. That shift moves them from procurement detail to schedule constraint: a project can have land, power, and capital approved and still wait on a transformer.

For AI specifically, this matters because accelerators sit on the same list as the electrical gear. Compute capacity cannot be added faster than the slowest delivered component, and the data places high-end accelerators alongside grid hardware rather than treating them as a separate fast-moving category. The bottleneck is not one supply chain but the coordination of several.

The data does not include actual lead-time figures, dates, or named manufacturers. It states the direction of change and the categories affected, and it points to industry groups and research firms as the sources for the underlying surveys. It also does not say whether lead times are currently rising, flat, or easing.
